shorts.title: Dem Senate Nominee To Susan Collins: "Shut Up" - Then Refuses To Apologize #Shorts
shorts.hook: "Shut Up": Dem Tells Susan Collins On Stage
shorts.narration: Folks, Maine had its final Senate debate, and the Democrat's big closing argument was two words. [beat] Troy Jackson told Susan Collins to "shut up." Collins had said a protester was one of his supporters, and Jackson answered with the debating skill of a kid at a family dinner. [sarcastic] Then he went on CNN with Dana Bash and said he's not going to apologize. [beat] Confidence! Pity it isn't a policy. [serious] The Good Book says, in Proverbs 15:1, "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger." [amused] Jackson read the second half and skipped the first. [beat] Maine voters wanted a Senator, and the Democrats sent them a heckler with a podium. So tell me, Democrats: if "shut up" is the answer, what exactly was the question? Subscribe, friends. Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Democratic nominee Troy Jackson told Republican Sen. Susan Collins to 'shut up' during the fourth and final Maine Senate debate, after Collins referred to a protester as one of Jackson's supporters.
Jackson told CNN's Dana Bash on Sunday, Oct. 18 that he is not going to apologize to Collins.
Collins is the Republican incumbent and Jackson the Democratic nominee in Maine's 2026 U.S. Senate race.

slides.text: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
slides.speaker: Proverbs 15:1 (KJV)

shorts.title: Trump To France: "Close Your Borders" As 1,800 Are Arrested #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, President Trump posted a warning to France on Truth Social: "France is burning!" He told Paris, "Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!" The Washington Examiner reports police arrested about 1,800 people in violent protests. [beat] [sarcastic] Now watch the usual crowd. For years, a secure border was a mean, scary idea. Now it's an urgent French policy debate, and the lecture never comes with an apology. [emphatic] Ecclesiastes 1:9 says, "there is no new thing under the sun." [beat] Including Washington experts discovering the problem after it moves to Europe. So here's my question for the folks in the comments: when the president warns an ally about its borders, is he wrong, or just early? Subscribe for the daily news.

claims.text: On Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, Trump urged France in a Truth Social post to tighten its borders, writing 'France is burning!' and 'Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!'
The Washington Examiner reports protests across France were violent and police arrested approximately 1,800 people.

shorts.title: Black Civic Group "Deeply Disappointed" After Talarico Cancels Event #Shorts
shorts.hook: Talarico's Black Outreach Draws A Rebuke
shorts.narration: Folks, Texas Democrat James Talarico promised $25 million to reach Black voters, and now a Black civic group is on the record. [beat] Fox News reports the Central Texas African American Civic Engagement Symposium had 325 people registered for an October 5 event that got canceled. The group says it understands his health came first, but it is, quote, "deeply disappointed," and cites "irrecoverable financial loss." [sarcastic] An anonymous Democratic operative told Fox, "We haven't received the money, but we're being told it's coming." [beat] The check is in the mail, folks. James 2:26 says, "faith without works is dead also." [amused] Apparently so is a pledge without a payment. Senate hopeful Ken Paxton can just watch. So, Democrats, where's the money? Subscribe, friends. Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: An Oct. 5 event with the Central Texas African American Civic Engagement Symposium (CT-AACES), with 325 confirmed registrants, was canceled during Talarico's roughly two-week absence from the campaign trail due to illness.
CT-AACES wrote to the campaign that 'While we understand Representative Talarico's health required priority, we are deeply disappointed' and cited 'irrecoverable financial loss'.

Talarico announced a $25 million pledge for outreach in Black communities at a July Houston town hall; an anonymous Austin-area Democratic operative told Fox News 'We haven't received the money, but we're being told it's coming.' The operative's claims are unverified.
The Texas Senate race is between Talarico and Republican nominee Ken Paxton.
